title: When Floating on Life's Troubled Sea
description: When Floating on Life's Troubled Sea in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 573 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Hope of Reunion above”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: When float-ing on life's trou-bled sea, By storms and tem-pests driven, Hope, with her ra-diant fin-ger, points To bright-er scenes in heaven.

lines: When floating on life's troubled sea,
Hope, with her radiant finger, points
She bids the storms of life to cease,
And in the wounded heart she pours
Her hallowed influence cheers life's hours
She guides us through this vale of tears,
She bids the anguished heart rejoice:
We still may hope to meet again

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
